The simulation models spray combustion in a cylindrical combustion chamber using a 2D axisymmetric computational domain.
The cylindrical chamber has a length of 0.2 m and a diameter of 0.1 m.
The initial chamber pressure is set to 101325 Pa.
The initial chamber gas temperature is set to 800 K with quiescent conditions where velocity is 0 m/s.
The initial gas composition in the chamber consists of an oxygen mass fraction of 0.233 and a nitrogen mass fraction of 0.767.
Standard k-epsilon turbulence modeling is applied to the continuous phase.
Liquid n-dodecane is injected at the center of the inlet boundary using a cone injection model.
The injection fuel temperature is 300 K and the mass flow rate is 0.002 kg/s.
The injected spray droplet sizes follow a Rosin-Rammler distribution with a mean diameter of 50 micrometers.
The spray full cone angle is set to 20 degrees.
Combustion chemistry uses a two-step global reaction mechanism for dodecane with JANAF thermodynamics.
The total physical simulation time is set to 0.05 s.
Adaptive time-stepping is enabled with a maximum Courant number of 0.7.
Simulation field results are written at an interval of every 0.001 s.
